market_holds: Spot 8.18 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-10 18:09 UTC), 1.9% above the 52-week low and 65% below the high, after -16.95% over 5 sessions and -27.67% over 20. Front-expiry straddle 15.3%, event-implied about 12.7% (ATM spread 48% of mid, so indicative only); median of 7 prior reactions 7.85%, 3 of 7 up, last three +7.85 / -3.11 / +8.36. Put/call OI 0.31 (call-heavy). Consensus about -$0.12 EPS and about $0.99m revenue (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-03); the quarter's numbers are immaterial against about $300m of liquidity (CFO, Lytham conference, reported 2026-10-04) on about 169m shares (EDGAR dei, 2026-08-07), so about $1.4bn of market value. The stock trades on one line: the FCC's lower-900 MHz PNT NPRM (WT 25-110). The 'stalled at OIRA' story is the stated consensus framing (preview headline 'a stalled FCC rule'), and the 19 Nov FCC agenda, announced 28-29 Oct, left the item off. The 2 Nov drop of 7-11% came after that agenda and the SpecTech Alliance opposition.
view: The release cannot carry the one thing that moves this stock. OIRA's live EO 12866 review list, read today, still shows RIN 3060-AM01 (Promoting the Development of PNT Technologies, WT Docket 25-110, proposed rule) as Pending Review, received 2026-03-02. That is more than eight months, while other FCC items received in October are moving through. So management will most likely repeat what it said in August and October: confident an NPRM will issue, timing outside its control, partnerships and spectrum-monetisation talks progressing. Everything in that list is public and is the preview's own framing. The quarter itself (about $1m of revenue, a GAAP loss driven by derivative accounting, cash burn against about $300m) is not a line the stock trades on. What is left is how the market reads a 'no-news' call after a 28% slide into the print. A modest relief bounce is as plausible as a capitulation leg if the tone on timing softens (for example a 2027 framing, or signs of an interagency objection). I can see no dated, undiscovered evidence that tips that balance either way.

recommendation.reason: The decisive line, OIRA clearance of the PNT NPRM, is confirmed unresolved as of the run day on reginfo.gov, and the stall is already the market's stated framing, the cause of the 2 Nov drop and of a 28% 20-day slide. The quarterly numbers are immaterial. I found no fresh evidence that the call will reveal something the price does not hold, in either direction.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A concrete regulatory datum in the release or call (OIRA clearance or an FCC agenda date would be a large up move; an admission of an interagency objection or a 2027 timeline would be a down move), or a signed spectrum lease, sale or buyback.

key_evidence.shows: FCC RIN 3060-AM01 PNT NPRM (WT 25-110) still Pending Review at OIRA, received 2026-03-02; other FCC items received Oct 2026 also listed
Preview frames Q3 as a stalled FCC rule; consensus -$0.12 EPS, about $0.99m revenue; about $300m liquidity; management says timing is outside its control
CFO at Lytham: NPRM in OIRA review, confident but no timetable; no capital raise for the network; partnerships, lease or sale discussions
Nov 19 FCC agenda covers drone, counter-UAS and in-flight spectrum items (450 MHz / 24 GHz), not lower 900 MHz
Nov 2 drop attributed to the SpecTech Alliance opposition and an agenda delay (AI-generated source, low reliability)
No 8-K since the 2026-08-11 earnings; only Form 4s and 144s through 2026-09-25 (tax-withholding sales)
House FY27 appropriations rider would bar the FCC from finalizing the 900 MHz reconfiguration; congressional opposition is long public

searched_and_found_nothing: Confirmation of the FY27 appropriations rider's fate
self_critique: A 28% slide into a print with call-heavy open interest and 9% short interest is the setup where a 'nothing new, still confident, $300m of runway' call produces an outsized relief bounce, as in Aug 2026 (+7.85%) and Mar 2026 (+8.36%). The opposite case is just as strong: a management that concedes a longer timeline breaks the last support. Either way the evidence does not choose between the two, which is why there is no call.
approach_notes: P4 and P6 helped: finding the one line (OIRA status) and checking it at the primary source (reginfo.gov) settled what the release can and cannot contain. P3's breadth of worker and customer sources does not apply to a pre-revenue regulatory story, and I skipped it deliberately.
